newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour defends trade union proposals.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour defends trade union proposals.

text.p: David Blunkett, employment and education spokesman for Britain's opposition Labour Party, on Wednesday defended his party's plans to require firms to recognise trade unions where this is backed by over 50 percent of the workforce.
"It is right people should be represented if more than 50 percent wish it do be done in that way," he told BBC Radio in an interview.
"The Americans, Europeans, every domestic country in the world accept there is an entitlement for people when a majority wish it, to be represented in the way they wish."
He said Labour's proposals were in one sense, among the most restricted in the democratic world.
"It's only a fairness we want to seek on hours and pay and holidays and on training. No-one in their right mind could describe that as a threat to anything."

On Tuesday, deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine attacked the proposals saying they would put power back in the unions' hands. He said Labour's relationship with unions would be a key factor in the May 1 election campaign.
